name: core_demo_ops_terminal
description: Ops core plan section 10 part 1: demo_ops_terminal through the network routes, captured before any ops-core edit.

scenario.scenario_brief: Ops demo: the Terminal close up. Fenlow Managed IT's field engineer Zainab is setting up remote support for Merrin & Sallow's file server, and Ama Owusu asks you to look at it the way an attacker's tools would. Read a scanner's report and a console's search in the Terminal view, test which findings are real, then see what a timed sign-in token and a shared screen give you, and what they do not. Authorised practice in a fictional office; nothing to break and no combat.
scenario.endGoal: Demo only: read the Terminal's reports, test the findings, and see what a token, a shared screen and a keyboard-only device do over a remote session.

objects.name: Things to try
objects.text:
Get in:
- Take the drop box to the server room and plug it into the port by the rack. The view opens as a Terminal.
- Sweep the network, then show the hosts as a table.
- Through the box, sign in to the backup PC with Zainab's token while it is fresh.
- Plug the keystroke device into the backup PC's socket.
The report:
- Scan the file server and check its storage service.
- Type help to find the console. Search, choose a module with use, ask for info, then tell Ama.
- Confirm all three, ask Zainab for her card, and use both cards.
- Switch to Panels and back, then tell Ama about your log.
Remote ways in:
- Ask Graham to share his screen, then ask Ama to have him end it.
- Watch the token run out. If it shows greyed out in your keyring, tell Ama.
- Unplug: click the box at its port, try a short form of unplug, then type the whole word.

voice.name: Autonoe
voice.style: Security lead on Merrin & Sallow's outsourced IT provider (Fenlow Managed IT), in her 40s, warm and practical. Speak with a consistent London and southern English accent throughout — do not shift to any other accent.

eventMappings.bark: Morning! Come and find me when you're ready.
This Terminal imitates a scanner and a console. Every name and number in it is invented. Zainab's token came with the box, and its clock is running.

eventMappings.bark: The same list Panels would show, as a table. Next, the backup PC.

eventMappings.condition: data.value === true && data.oldValue !== true && globalVars.needs_console_done !== true
eventMappings.bark: You're on the backup PC with a token, no password. It only lasts a few minutes. Try the keystroke device on its socket.

eventMappings.condition: data.value === true && data.oldValue !== true && globalVars.scan_check_done !== true
eventMappings.bark: That device needs someone signed in at its keyboard. A remote session doesn't count. Now scan the file server.

eventMappings.bark: Three findings, each with a scanner's write-up and reference ids. Any of them could be a false alarm. They all read the same.

data.value === true && data.oldValue !== true && globalVars.step_up_done !== true
eventMappings.bark: Two real, one false, and the false one says why. The write-ups didn't tell you that. Testing did.
That's a user session. The settings finding needs one before it will work.
A user session first, then an administrator's on top of it.
You're on Graham's own screen because he let you in. It shows as Administrator because he is one. It's still his session.
Tokens run out. The session ended on the clock, and the token won't open it again.
The spare port. Its token's clock starts now. Sign in to the backup PC with the spare token.

eventMappings.bark: In the Terminal, unplugging needs the whole word, so a slip of the keys can't do it. It also ended every session through the box.
